text:
Help me build a super strength simulator. I’ve got a dinosaur character (here in marketable plush form). Assuming he’s totally indestructible and inexhaustible, I want to have him do physics simulations of famous feats of strength. The goal is to understand the physics of how much force he’d have to output. Like, if this guy was as physically strong as the strongest recorded human, or various superheroes, up to effectively infinite strength, what would the physics look like? What would he be able to lift or throw? What effect would he have on his surroundings by just moving?

args.prompt:
PROJECT: We are building a physics simulator for a cartoon anthropomorphic dinosaur character who is indestructible and never tires. The user picks a strength level (from "strongest recorded human" through comic-book superheroes up to effectively infinite) and the sim computes the physics of famous feats: lift forces, throw speeds and ranges, recoil, ground failure under his feet, blast/seismic effects of punches/stomps/claps, etc. Your data feeds a JavaScript physics engine directly, so every number must be correct, sourced, and in SI.
The user is a professional critic who values factual accuracy above all. If something cannot be verified, say so and mark it; never invent a number or a citation. Today's date is 2026-10-09: sports records may have been broken recently (e.g., a 511 kg strongman deadlift by Raul Flores was reported in Sept 2026), so always search for the current state, not your memory.
Tools: use ToolSearch with query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" to load web tools, then search and open real pages. Do not edit any files or repositories.
Output conventions: value_si in SI base units (kg, m, s, N, Pa, J, m/s, m^2, K). Metric tonne = 1000 kg. Short ton = 907.18474 kg; long ton = 1016.047 kg; lb = 0.45359237 kg. When a source says "tons", determine which ton it means and say so in notes. Use low_si/high_si when the honest answer is a range. key must be a unique snake_case id.

TOPIC: Strongest recorded humans and the human biomechanics numbers needed to calibrate a muscle model.
Collect (current as of 2026-10-09; give person, date, venue, and status verified/disputed/claimed):
A) Lift records: strongman deadlift WR; raw and equipped powerlifting deadlift WRs (name the federation); partial-range lifts (silver dollar / 18-inch deadlift record; heaviest back lift - Gregg Ernst and others; Paul Anderson's claimed 1957 back lift, marked claimed/disputed); Olympic weightlifting clean & jerk and snatch WRs (note the IWF 2025 weight-class change and how records/world standards were reset); log press WR; atlas stone WR; heaviest squat WR.
B) Pull/drag records: heaviest aircraft pulled by one person (Guinness), heaviest vehicle/truck pulled, any "heaviest weight held/supported" record.
C) Throw/speed calibration: shot put WR (and implement mass 7.26 kg), hammer throw WR, javelin WR, discus WR, fastest recorded baseball pitch (mph and m/s), fastest measured human punch (fist speed, m/s) with source quality, highest standing vertical jump on record, standing long jump record, Usain Bolt peak running speed (m/s).
D) Biomechanics: body segment mass fractions (hand, forearm, upper arm, whole arm, foot, shank, thigh, whole leg) from Winter or Dempster with citation; Hill force-velocity model curvature parameter a/F0 (typical value and range) and the equation form; typical max limb endpoint speeds: elite punch fist speed, pitching hand/ball release speed, kick foot speed, vertical jump takeoff velocity for elite jumpers; peak ground reaction force in elite sprinting (multiples of body weight); barefoot plantar contact area of one adult foot standing (m^2); palm contact area of one adult hand (m^2).
Give each item as one fact. Include short notes on what the record actually measures (full range vs partial, equipped vs raw, suits/straps), because the sim must not overstate human ability.

Return every item as a fact. List anything you could not find under gaps.

text: Returned facts: 57 (e.g. marvel_handbook_ton_unit; ohotmu_deluxe_class100_definition), gaps: 19.

TOPIC: Canon-stated strength figures and famous strength feats from comics, myth, and fiction.

TOPIC: Environment and physical constants for the engine.
A) Ground surfaces - for each: ultimate bearing capacity (Pa) for a small (~0.1 m^2) footing near the surface, with the allowable/presumptive value too if that's what references give (say which); shear strength (Pa); a reasonable friction coefficient for a scaly foot with keratin claws (an estimate, with reasoning). Surfaces: loose dry sand, dense sand/gravel, soft clay, stiff clay, asphalt pavement on compacted base, concrete slab (give f'c range and note punching shear of slab-on-grade), intact granite bedrock (UCS range and how bearing capacity of rock under a small punch relates to UCS - confinement factor), structural steel plate (yield), sea ice/freshwater ice (compressive strength).
B) Atmosphere (ISA sea level): density, pressure, temperature, speed of sound, ratio of specific heats, density scale height for the lower atmosphere, mass of the atmospheric column per m^2.
C) Earth: standard gravity, mean radius, escape velocity at surface, circular orbital velocity at surface.
D) Energy references: TNT equivalence (J per tonne); M67 grenade explosive mass; GBU-43 MOAB yield; Hiroshima yield; Castle Bravo; Tsar Bomba; Tunguska (range); 1883 Krakatoa (range); Chicxulub impact energy (range); Sun's luminosity; Earth's gravitational binding energy. Also the xkcd What If #1 "Relativistic Baseball" scenario (0.9c pitch) - the energy figure it gives, as a sanity reference.
E) Seismic: the Gutenberg-Richter energy-magnitude relation (exact form, units) with citation; seismic efficiency used for impacts (Collins, Melosh & Marcus 2005 Earth Impact Effects Program value, and the literature range).
F) Blast: the Kinney & Graham (1985) scaled-distance peak overpressure formula (exact equation, ambient pressure scaling, validity) and peak-overpressure damage thresholds: typical window breakage, eardrum rupture (50% threshold), residential collapse, reinforced concrete severe damage, lung damage/lethality. Also a typical sonic boom overpressure (e.g., Concorde) in Pa.
G) Cratering: the Collins, Melosh & Marcus (2005) transient crater diameter formula for impacts (exact equation, variables, units) and the simple-crater final diameter relation.
H) Aerothermal: stagnation temperature formula for a calorically perfect gas, and a caution on its validity above ~Mach 5-6 (dissociation); a reference figure for peak heating temperatures on reentry (e.g., Space Shuttle).
Cite textbooks, standards, agency pages, or peer-reviewed papers.

Today's date is 2026-10-09: sports records may have been broken recently (e.g., a 511 kg strongman deadlift by Raul Flores was reported in Sept 2026), so always search for the current state, not your memory.

When a source says "tons", determine which ton it means and say so in notes. Use low_si/high_si when the honest answer is a range. key must be a unique snake_case id.

PROJECT: We are building a physics simulator for a cartoon anthropomorphic dinosaur character who is indestructible and never tires. The user picks a strength level (from "strongest recorded human" through comic-book superheroes up to effectively infinite) and the sim computes the physics of famous feats: lift forces, throw speeds and ranges, recoil, ground failure under his feet, blast/seismic effects of punches/stomps/claps, etc. Your data feeds a JavaScript physics engine directly, so every number must be correct, sourced, and in SI.
The user is a professional critic who values factual accuracy above all. If something cannot be verified, say so and mark it; never invent a number or a citation. Today's date is 2026-10-09: sports records may have been broken recently (e.g., a 511 kg strongman deadlift by Raul Flores was reported in Sept 2026), so always search for the current state, not your memory.
Tools: use ToolSearch with query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" to load web tools, then search and open real pages. Do not edit any files or repositories.
Output conventions: value_si in SI base units (kg, m, s, N, Pa, J, m/s, m^2, K). Metric tonne = 1000 kg. Short ton = 907.18474 kg; long ton = 1016.047 kg; lb = 0.45359237 kg. When a source says "tons", determine which ton it means and say so in notes. Use low_si/high_si when the honest answer is a range. key must be a unique snake_case id.

You are verifying a researcher's dataset for topic "Superhero / myth strength canon".
LENS: SKEPTIC. Assume the researcher made mistakes. Recompute every unit conversion (lb/kg, short/long/metric tons, psi/Pa, mph/m/s). Hunt for: misattribution; claimed or disputed feats presented as verified; partial-range or equipped lifts presented as full-range raw; allowable bearing capacity presented as ultimate; fan calculations presented as canon; implausible drag coefficients; ranges collapsed to falsely precise points; wrong issue numbers or years. Search the web to settle each doubt. Default to "unverifiable" when you cannot settle it.

TOPIC: Canon-stated strength figures and famous strength feats from comics, myth, and fiction.
A) Marvel: the Official Handbook of the Marvel Universe strength-class system. B) Specific canon feats with an in-universe stated number: Secret Wars #4 (1984) Hulk holding the mountain range (verify the exact stated figure and wording); All-Star Superman #3 (2006) Superman's stated lift (verify "200 quintillion tons" or correct it); any DC or Marvel feat where the text states a mass/force (e.g., Superman moving the Earth or Moon, Hercules towing Manhattan, Thor and the Midgard Serpent). For each: issue, year, page/panel if findable, exact stated figure, and what object.
C) Famous depicted-but-unquantified feats worth simulating: Action Comics #1 (1938) Superman lifting the car on the cover (identify the car type and a realistic mass range for a late-1930s sedan as an estimate), Saitama's serious punch in One-Punch Man (no stated value - mark not_quantified), Superman catching/lifting airliners, etc.
D) Myth and legend: Atlas holding up the heavens; Thor lifting Utgarda-Loki's cat (Prose Edda, Gylfaginning - which chapter, what he achieved); Samson and the temple pillars (Judges 16 verse refs); Sun Wukong's staff Ruyi Jingu Bang stated weight (13,500 jin? verify, chapter) with the historical jin-to-kg conversion and resulting mass range; Milo of Croton carrying a bull; Heracles if there is a quantifiable feat.
Rules: Fan wikis (VS Battles, Fandom) and fan calculations are NOT sources for canon numbers; you may use them only as pointers, and the claim must be confirmed in a primary text or a reputable secondary source (publisher sites, reputable press, scans quoted in reputable outlets, Wikipedia with citations). Status values: canon_stated (number given in the work), not_quantified (shown but no number), claimed (number appears only in secondary/fan sources). If you cannot confirm, say "cannot verify" in notes and use status claimed.

PROJECT: We are building a physics simulator for a cartoon anthropomorphic dinosaur character who is indestructible and never tires. The user picks a strength level (from "strongest recorded human" through comic-book superheroes up to effectively infinite) and the sim computes the physics of famous feats: lift forces, throw speeds and ranges, recoil, ground failure under his feet, blast/seismic effects of punches/stomps/claps, etc. Your data feeds a JavaScript physics engine directly, so every number must be correct, sourced, and in SI.
The user is a professional critic who values factual accuracy above all. If something cannot be verified, say so and mark it; never invent a number or a citation. Today's date is 2026-10-09: sports records may have been broken recently (e.g., a 511 kg strongman deadlift by Raul Flores was reported in Sept 2026), so always search for the current state, not your memory.
Tools: use ToolSearch with query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" to load web tools, then search and open real pages. Do not edit any files or repositories.

The researcher was asked:
TOPIC: Physical data for an object library the dinosaur can lift or throw.
For each object give: mass (value_si, with low/high if it varies), typical dimensions (L x W x H in m, in notes), frontal/cross-section area estimate for a thrown object in m^2, drag coefficient estimate (state the shape assumption; note tumbling bluff bodies are ~1.0 and supersonic spheres ~0.9-1.0), the material at the grip point and its crush/yield/compressive strength in Pa (e.g., car body sheet steel, aircraft aluminium skin, granite), and a one-line structural note on what happens if you try to lift the whole thing from one hand-sized contact point.
Objects: baseball; men's shot put; max-weight bowling ball; average adult human; Steinway Model D grand piano; a typical motorcycle; Toyota Corolla curb mass; Ford F-150 curb mass; full-size Type C school bus; US semi truck at the 80,000 lb legal max; M1A2 SEPv3 Abrams tank; adult blue whale (typical and largest recorded); EMD SD70ACe locomotive; Boeing 747-400 (operating empty and max takeoff); Airbus A380 max takeoff; Space Shuttle full stack at liftoff; Statue of Liberty (copper skin + steel framework + total); Eiffel Tower (iron structure and total); RMS Titanic displacement; Nimitz-class carrier full-load displacement; Empire State Building total mass estimate (state method/uncertainty); Great Pyramid of Giza mass; Mount Everest mass estimate (state the method and the definition of where the mountain ends, give a range); a typical cumulus cloud's water mass; the Moon; Earth; the Sun.
Prefer manufacturer specs, official agencies (NASA, USGS, NPS), and reputable references. Mark rough estimates as status estimate.

Cite textbooks, standards, agency pages, or peer-reviewed papers.

PROJECT: We are building a physics simulator for a cartoon anthropomorphic dinosaur character who is indestructible and never tires. The user picks a strength level (from "strongest recorded human" through comic-book superheroes up to effectively infinite) and the sim computes the physics of famous feats: lift forces, throw speeds and ranges, recoil, ground failure under his feet, blast/seismic effects of punches/stomps/claps, etc. Your data feeds a JavaScript physics engine directly, so every number must be correct, sourced, and in SI.
The user is a professional critic who values factual accuracy above all. If something cannot be verified, say so and mark it; never invent a number or a citation. Today's date is 2026-10-09: sports records may have been broken recently (e.g., a 511 kg strongman deadlift by Raul Flores was reported in Sept 2026), so always search for the current state, not your memory.
Tools: use ToolSearch with query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" to load web tools, then search and open real pages. Do not edit any files or repositories.
Output conventions: value_si in SI base units (kg, m, s, N, Pa, J, m/s, m^2, K). Metric tonne = 1000 kg. Short ton = 907.18474 kg; long ton = 1016.047 kg; lb = 0.45359237 kg. When a source says "tons", determine which ton it means and say so in notes. Use low_si/high_si when the honest answer is a range. key must be a unique snake_case id.

You are verifying a researcher's dataset for topic "Ground, air, energy, blast and seismic constants".
LENS: SKEPTIC. Assume the researcher made mistakes. Recompute every unit conversion (lb/kg, short/long/metric tons, psi/Pa, mph/m/s). Hunt for: misattribution; claimed or disputed feats presented as verified; partial-range or equipped lifts presented as full-range raw; allowable bearing capacity presented as ultimate; fan calculations presented as canon; implausible drag coefficients; ranges collapsed to falsely precise points; wrong issue numbers or years. Search the web to settle each doubt. Default to "unverifiable" when you cannot settle it.

The researcher was asked:
TOPIC: Environment and physical constants for the engine.
A) Ground surfaces - for each: ultimate bearing capacity (Pa) for a small (~0.1 m^2) footing near the surface, with the allowable/presumptive value too if that's what references give (say which); shear strength (Pa); a reasonable friction coefficient for a scaly foot with keratin claws (an estimate, with reasoning). Surfaces: loose dry sand, dense sand/gravel, soft clay, stiff clay, asphalt pavement on compacted base, concrete slab (give f'c range and note punching shear of slab-on-grade), intact granite bedrock (UCS range and how bearing capacity of rock under a small punch relates to UCS - confinement factor), structural steel plate (yield), sea ice/freshwater ice (compressive strength).
B) Atmosphere (ISA sea level): density, pressure, temperature, speed of sound, ratio of specific heats, density scale height for the lower atmosphere, mass of the atmospheric column per m^2.
C) Earth: standard gravity, mean radius, escape velocity at surface, circular orbital velocity at surface.
D) Energy references: TNT equivalence (J per tonne); M67 grenade explosive mass; GBU-43 MOAB yield; Hiroshima yield; Castle Bravo; Tsar Bomba; Tunguska (range); 1883 Krakatoa (range); Chicxulub impact energy (range); Sun's luminosity; Earth's gravitational binding energy. Also the xkcd What If #1 "Relativistic Baseball" scenario (0.9c pitch) - the energy figure it gives, as a sanity reference.
E) Seismic: the Gutenberg-Richter energy-magnitude relation (exact form, units) with citation; seismic efficiency used for impacts (Collins, Melosh & Marcus 2005 Earth Impact Effects Program value, and the literature range).
F) Blast: the Kinney & Graham (1985) scaled-distance peak overpressure formula (exact equation, ambient pressure scaling, validity) and peak-overpressure damage thresholds: typical window breakage, eardrum rupture (50% threshold), residential collapse, reinforced concrete severe damage, lung damage/lethality. Also a typical sonic boom overpressure (e.g., Concorde) in Pa.
G) Cratering: the Collins, Melosh & Marcus (2005) transient crater diameter formula for impacts (exact equation, variables, units) and the simple-crater final diameter relation.
H) Aerothermal: stagnation temperature formula for a calorically perfect gas, and a caution on its validity above ~Mach 5-6 (dissociation); a reference figure for peak heating temperatures on reentry (e.g., Space Shuttle).
Cite textbooks, standards, agency pages, or peer-reviewed papers.

PROJECT: We are building a physics simulator for a cartoon anthropomorphic dinosaur character who is indestructible and never tires. The user picks a strength level (from "strongest recorded human" through comic-book superheroes up to effectively infinite) and the sim computes the physics of famous feats: lift forces, throw speeds and ranges, recoil, ground failure under his feet, blast/seismic effects of punches/stomps/claps, etc. Your data feeds a JavaScript physics engine directly, so every number must be correct, sourced, and in SI.
The user is a professional critic who values factual accuracy above all. If something cannot be verified, say so and mark it; never invent a number or a citation. Today's date is 2026-10-09: sports records may have been broken recently (e.g., a 511 kg strongman deadlift by Raul Flores was reported in Sept 2026), so always search for the current state, not your memory.

PROJECT: We are building a physics simulator for a cartoon anthropomorphic dinosaur character who is indestructible and never tires. The user picks a strength level (from "strongest recorded human" through comic-book superheroes up to effectively infinite) and the sim computes the physics of famous feats: lift forces, throw speeds and ranges, recoil, ground failure under his feet, blast/seismic effects of punches/stomps/claps, etc. Your data feeds a JavaScript physics engine directly, so every number must be correct, sourced, and in SI.
The user is a professional critic who values factual accuracy above all. If something cannot be verified, say so and mark it; never invent a number or a citation. Today's date is 2026-10-09: sports records may have been broken recently (e.g., a 511 kg strongman deadlift by Raul Flores was reported in Sept 2026), so always search for the current state, not your memory.
Tools: use ToolSearch with query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" to load web tools, then search and open real pages. Do not edit any files or repositories.
Output conventions: value_si in SI base units (kg, m, s, N, Pa, J, m/s, m^2, K). Metric tonne = 1000 kg. Short ton = 907.18474 kg; long ton = 1016.047 kg; lb = 0.45359237 kg. When a source says "tons", determine which ton it means and say so in notes. Use low_si/high_si when the honest answer is a range. key must be a unique snake_case id.

You are the final editor for topic "Object library: masses, sizes, drag, materials". Below are a researcher's dataset and the verdicts of two independent verifiers (a source checker and a skeptic). Produce the FINAL dataset:
- Apply corrections both verifiers agree on.
- Where verifiers disagree with each other or with the researcher, settle it yourself with a targeted web search and say how in notes.
- Downgrade status where a claim could not be confirmed (verified -> claimed/estimate; canon_stated -> claimed). Never upgrade without evidence.
- Fill items the verifiers listed as missing if you can source them quickly; otherwise list them in gaps.
- Keep sources for every fact (url required).

ORIGINAL REQUEST:
TOPIC: Physical data for an object library the dinosaur can lift or throw.
For each object give: mass (value_si, with low/high if it varies), typical dimensions (L x W x H in m, in notes), frontal/cross-section area estimate for a thrown object in m^2, drag coefficient estimate (state the shape assumption; note tumbling bluff bodies are ~1.0 and supersonic spheres ~0.9-1.0), the material at the grip point and its crush/yield/compressive strength in Pa (e.g., car body sheet steel, aircraft aluminium skin, granite), and a one-line structural note on what happens if you try to lift the whole thing from one hand-sized contact point.
Objects: baseball; men's shot put; max-weight bowling ball; average adult human; Steinway Model D grand piano; a typical motorcycle; Toyota Corolla curb mass; Ford F-150 curb mass; full-size Type C school bus; US semi truck at the 80,000 lb legal max; M1A2 SEPv3 Abrams tank; adult blue whale (typical and largest recorded); EMD SD70ACe locomotive; Boeing 747-400 (operating empty and max takeoff); Airbus A380 max takeoff; Space Shuttle full stack at liftoff; Statue of Liberty (copper skin + steel framework + total); Eiffel Tower (iron structure and total); RMS Titanic displacement; Nimitz-class carrier full-load displacement; Empire State Building total mass estimate (state method/uncertainty); Great Pyramid of Giza mass; Mount Everest mass estimate (state the method and the definition of where the mountain ends, give a range); a typical cumulus cloud's water mass; the Moon; Earth; the Sun.
Prefer manufacturer specs, official agencies (NASA, USGS, NPS), and reputable references. Mark rough estimates as status estimate.

PROJECT: We are building a physics simulator for a cartoon anthropomorphic dinosaur character who is indestructible and never tires. The user picks a strength level (from "strongest recorded human" through comic-book superheroes up to effectively infinite) and the sim computes the physics of famous feats: lift forces, throw speeds and ranges, recoil, ground failure under his feet, blast/seismic effects of punches/stomps/claps, etc. Your data feeds a JavaScript physics engine directly, so every number must be correct, sourced, and in SI.
The user is a professional critic who values factual accuracy above all. If something cannot be verified, say so and mark it; never invent a number or a citation. Today's date is 2026-10-09: sports records may have been broken recently (e.g., a 511 kg strongman deadlift by Raul Flores was reported in Sept 2026), so always search for the current state, not your memory.
Tools: use ToolSearch with query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" to load web tools, then search and open real pages. Do not edit any files or repositories.
Output conventions: value_si in SI base units (kg, m, s, N, Pa, J, m/s, m^2, K). Metric tonne = 1000 kg. Short ton = 907.18474 kg; long ton = 1016.047 kg; lb = 0.45359237 kg. When a source says "tons", determine which ton it means and say so in notes. Use low_si/high_si when the honest answer is a range. key must be a unique snake_case id.

You are the final editor for topic "Ground, air, energy, blast and seismic constants". Below are a researcher's dataset and the verdicts of two independent verifiers (a source checker and a skeptic). Produce the FINAL dataset:
- Apply corrections both verifiers agree on.
- Where verifiers disagree with each other or with the researcher, settle it yourself with a targeted web search and say how in notes.
- Downgrade status where a claim could not be confirmed (verified -> claimed/estimate; canon_stated -> claimed). Never upgrade without evidence.
- Fill items the verifiers listed as missing if you can source them quickly; otherwise list them in gaps.
- Keep sources for every fact (url required).

ORIGINAL REQUEST:
TOPIC: Environment and physical constants for the engine.
A) Ground surfaces - for each: ultimate bearing capacity (Pa) for a small (~0.1 m^2) footing near the surface, with the allowable/presumptive value too if that's what references give (say which); shear strength (Pa); a reasonable friction coefficient for a scaly foot with keratin claws (an estimate, with reasoning). Surfaces: loose dry sand, dense sand/gravel, soft clay, stiff clay, asphalt pavement on compacted base, concrete slab (give f'c range and note punching shear of slab-on-grade), intact granite bedrock (UCS range and how bearing capacity of rock under a small punch relates to UCS - confinement factor), structural steel plate (yield), sea ice/freshwater ice (compressive strength).
B) Atmosphere (ISA sea level): density, pressure, temperature, speed of sound, ratio of specific heats, density scale height for the lower atmosphere, mass of the atmospheric column per m^2.
C) Earth: standard gravity, mean radius, escape velocity at surface, circular orbital velocity at surface.
D) Energy references: TNT equivalence (J per tonne); M67 grenade explosive mass; GBU-43 MOAB yield; Hiroshima yield; Castle Bravo; Tsar Bomba; Tunguska (range); 1883 Krakatoa (range); Chicxulub impact energy (range); Sun's luminosity; Earth's gravitational binding energy. Also the xkcd What If #1 "Relativistic Baseball" scenario (0.9c pitch) - the energy figure it gives, as a sanity reference.
E) Seismic: the Gutenberg-Richter energy-magnitude relation (exact form, units) with citation; seismic efficiency used for impacts (Collins, Melosh & Marcus 2005 Earth Impact Effects Program value, and the literature range).
F) Blast: the Kinney & Graham (1985) scaled-distance peak overpressure formula (exact equation, ambient pressure scaling, validity) and peak-overpressure damage thresholds: typical window breakage, eardrum rupture (50% threshold), residential collapse, reinforced concrete severe damage, lung damage/lethality. Also a typical sonic boom overpressure (e.g., Concorde) in Pa.
G) Cratering: the Collins, Melosh & Marcus (2005) transient crater diameter formula for impacts (exact equation, variables, units) and the simple-crater final diameter relation.
H) Aerothermal: stagnation temperature formula for a calorically perfect gas, and a caution on its validity above ~Mach 5-6 (dissociation); a reference figure for peak heating temperatures on reentry (e.g., Space Shuttle).
Cite textbooks, standards, agency pages, or peer-reviewed papers.

text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - The user wants help building a super-strength simulator for their dinosaur character, Rex (a plush-style kaiju-dino image was attached). Assumptions: totally indestructible and inexhaustible. The simulator should run physics on famous feats of strength, show how much force he'd have to output, and cover strength levels from the strongest recorded human through various superheroes up to effectively infinite. Questions to answer: what he could lift or throw, and what effect he'd have on his surroundings just by moving.
   - Later message: "His name is Rex by the way. Basic I know but still. I'm going to bed so just get as far as you can." So: name him Rex and work autonomously as far as possible, without asking questions.
   - User preferences, to keep applying: act as a professional critic, not a cheerleader; loyalty only to factual accuracy, clarity and intellectual honesty; say "I don't know" or "I cannot verify this" when information is lacking; admit mistakes briefly; polite and professional; don't argue for the sake of it; no filler niceties; "Always run in ADHD Mode". The i-have-adhd skill rules persist: lead with the action, number steps, cap lists at 5, no preamble or recap, restate state, give specific time estimates, end with one concrete next action.
   - Harness constraints:
     - Develop on branch `claude/dinosaur-strength-physics-8o13ft`, then commit and push with `git push -u origin <branch>`. Do NOT create a PR unless asked.
     - Commit messages end with:
       Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
       Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01SsJhZqR8L4f82P9Dfpr4zn
     - Don't include model identifiers in artifacts or code.
     - Ultracode is on: use workflows for substantive tasks.
     - The workflow concurrency cap is 2 agents (4 CPUs).

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Two-body push model: an internal force F pushes bodies A and B apart over a stroke d, each side with a resistance R (Infinity means immovable; RA can be a function of F). Comic mode uses a relativistic closed form with constant force (xOfT, bisection on t). Real mode uses the Hill force–velocity curve (a/F0 = 0.25) with an implicit backward-Euler integrator that bisects the new relative speed to adjacent doubles, an Fcap option, F0 clamped to (RA+RB) + 1e6·max(m)·vmax²/d, and tracking of workA/workB/vBmax.
   - Comic calibration (calibrateComic): a per-move constant share comicFrac, chosen so comic equals real at record-human strength (511 kg). `comicAtLeastReal` makes comic never weaker than real; the real run is skipped once the comic result passes the real cap.
   - Muscle parameters (MUSCLE):
     - throwPush {vmax 35, forceFrac 0.523}
     - throwWhip {84.6, 0.3}
     - punch and clap {17, 0.3}
     - jump {12, 1.4}
     - stomp {16, 0.5}
     - run {atCal 12.42, cap 17.9}
     - k 0.25
     - vmax scales linearly with size s.
   - Body: 2 m, 180 kg baseline with isometric scaling. Foot 0.045 s² m² per foot, palm 0.015 s², front area 0.8 s², top area 0.3 s², Cd 1. handEff 0.022m, whipEff 0.003m, legEff 0.061m, feetMass 0.029m, digArea 0.2 s². Strokes: throw 1.6s, whip 2.2s, punch 0.7s, leg 0.5s, stomp 0.6s, clap 0.5s. Release height 0.9H.
   - anchorCapacity:
     - N(F) = mA g + F sinθ + mB g cos²θ.
     - R1 = (μ(mA g + mB g cos²θ) + dig + mB g sinθ cosθ)/(cosθ − μ sinθ).
     - R2 = (μ Nmax + dig)/cosθ + mB g sinθ.
     - R = min(R1, R2).
     - Rslide(F) = F − cosθ·max(0, F cosθ − mB g sinθ cosθ − μ min(N(F), Nmax) − dig).
     - Bolted gives Infinity.
   - Granular ground scales: q_ult(B) = qult·B/Bref (Bref 0.316 m). Poncelet resistance A(q + kρv²) with k = 1. Jump feet use quasi-steady terminal speed (relativistic: u = √(f/c), vt = u/√(1+(u/c)²), p = m u). Leg lock: p = pA − pB. Hold-back candidates for jumps and throws.
   - Flight: RK4 over a round Earth with an exponential atmosphere (Hs = p0/(ρ0 g)), Cd(Mach) interpolated between Cd and CdSup (0.8 to 1.2 Mach), Kepler conicTo above 150 km and for vacuum, radial fallback, Hill-sphere limit R_HILL 1.5e9 m (leavesHill), escape/orbit/timedOut flags, vacuumApex Kepler formula.
   - Crater: Collins et al. 2005 eq. 21 plus eq. 27 (held at 3.2 km across the switch); above 20 km/s, a same-energy, same-density impactor at 20 km/s; planetScale when D > R_E.
   - Other models:
     - Gutenberg–Richter magnitude with seismic efficiency 1e-4.
     - Kinney–Graham blast radii, capped at πR_E.
     - Equilibrium-air stagnation table STAG_EQ.
     - EARTH_BIND = 2.49e32 J.
     - Relativistic pull time t = √(2x/a + (x/c)²).
   - Status labels: verified, canon_stated, reported (new: press/review-only canon), estimate, claimed, disputed, not_quantified.
   - Artifact page contract: inline engine, data and image; Google Fonts (Big Shoulders Display, Atkinson Hyperlegible, IBM Plex Mono); theme tokens for light and dark; phone width.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - /home/user/dino-strength-sim/ is the working project (primary dev location).
     - src/engine.js: the physics. Functions:
       - makeBody, qultFor, momentumToV/KE, vToMomentum, keFromV, xOfT, hill
       - pushApart(o) (RA may be a function; comic closed form; drag side), pushApartHill(o, RAf, RB, cA, cB)
       - anchorCapacity (returns R, Rslide, limit, Nmax, N, normalCapped)
       - rhoAt, STAG_EQ, stagnationT(v), stagnationTIdeal, cdAt, conicTo (returns p, e, f0 too), fly(oIn), vacuumApex, craterDiameter, seismicMagnitude, kgRatio, overpressureAt, blastRadius, penetrationDepth
       - sizeVmax, actionForce, comicAtLeastReal, lift (canLift tolerance 1e-9), throwStyle, throwOnce/throwObject, jumpOnce/jump, stompOnce/stomp (bolted → RA Infinity; no crater on groundHolds), punchOnce/punch, clapOnce/clap, sprint (cantStand 'too weak to sprint'; t100 with drag atanh), pull (relativistic t10m and vEnd), threshold, calibrateComic.
       - Exports include the *Once functions.
     - src/app.html: the page.
       - Hero; strength dial (slider log10 kg 1–34, label "10³⁴ kg (about 5,000 Suns)", tier chips).
       - Collapsible "Settings" details (muscle mode, surface, comic ground, size chips, height, mass, anchor; summary #setup-sum; open on desktop ≥ 920 px).
       - Tabs (role tablist, keyboard arrows/Home/End), bay (role tabpanel), #bay-live aria-live.
       - Bay functions bayLift/Throw/Jump/Stomp/Punch/Clap/Sprint/Pull, blastBlock, quakeChip, logBars (stacked labels on narrow widths, aria-label values), trajectoryChart(path, ghost, label, apexH) with dashed ghost, logMeter.
       - Strength ladder: thresholdDefs and computeThresholds, time-sliced at 25 ms and cached by settings key thKey; renderLadder with wrapped labels, hit rects, arrow "now" marker, focus restore.
       - Feats (STATUS_LABEL map), runFeat (sets mode first; setKg nudge +1e-12; jump60 solve).
       - Model/sources table, state validation (VALID map), localStorage key 'rex-lab-v1', mathOpen persistence, renderBay(keepControls) keeping .bay-controls during slider drag, resize redraw.
       - Defaults: Hulk & Thor tier (100 short tons), comic, concrete, friction, Throw, car, 45°.
       - nb() keeps numbers and units together with NBSP.
     - src/data.js: generated by build-data.py. Do not hand-edit.
     - src/static-data.js: heights with sources, and the assumptions text (updated with corrections).
     - build-data.py: builds data.js from research/final-*.json. Contains tiers (with lift field), surfaces, 32 objects, energy refs, overpressure thresholds, speeds, calibration, 23 feats, source rows (134), the REPORTED set, and RANK.
     - build.js: inlines engine, data and the base64 image into dist/index.html.
     - test/calibration.js: assertions for records, monotonicity, real caps, comic ≥ real, flight, blast, quake, stagnation T, and relativistic pull. All pass.
     - test/sweep.js: 5,184 contexts, 0 problems, about 500 s.
     - test/shots.js: Playwright screenshots at 1280 light and 390 dark; writes dist/preview.html; waits 4000 ms.
     - test/fit-v2.js: fitting script.
     - assets/dino.jpg: cropped image.
     - research/: final-*.json, verdicts-*.json, audit-final.json, audit2-final.json, audit2-findings.txt, audit3-final.json.
   - /home/user/lodge-docs/rex-strength-lab/: committed copy of src, test, build scripts, research/final-*.json, assets, dist/index.html, README.md and .gitignore (shots/, dist/preview.html). Commits cb1296f and c22dc45 are pushed to origin claude/dinosaur-strength-physics-8o13ft.
   - Artifact source: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/6435a7db-fe21-5f3b-bca9-e49ba2609387/scratchpad/rex-strength-lab.html (a copy of dist/index.html). Published at https://claude.ai/artifact/YFpbHtX8tM2Qwffd6znbZP (v2). Republish by publishing the same file path.
   - Scratchpad also holds audit2-args.json (the findings list) and workflow scratch dirs.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Workflow concurrency was only 2, so runs were slow. I worked in parallel instead of waiting.
   - Engine audit 1 found: ladder threshold N vs kg units; Hill integrator stalling; jump dropping feet momentum; stomp holes deeper than Earth; recoil overstated; flat throws of unliftable objects; energy from velocity giving Infinity or NaN; flat-g vacuum apex; terminal speed area mismatch; crater at relativistic speeds; ideal-gas temperatures; blast and quake domain issues; Cd constant; "fusion at 1% c"; sand q not scaling with width; sprint labels; comic ground in sprint; anchor discontinuity. All fixed in engine v2 and the UI.
   - Comic jump was non-monotone at the 0.99c foot cap. Fixed with the relativistic terminal-speed formula.
   - Sweep NaNs at F = ∞ (Eground, footShare, sinkRatio). Fixed with guards.
   - Audit 2 (77 findings): fixed the 1% light-speed formatting, the Suns label, real ∞ jump, Hill precision, throw and jump hold-back, Rslide, pull relativity, bolted stomp, comic-ground craters, Atlas rounding (setKg), comic ≥ real, 90° throws, contrast, tabs aria, slider drag, the ladder, and data text (D1–D17).
   - Mistake: I launched the verification workflow with placeholder args. I stopped it (TaskStop), the scriptPath relaunch was rejected, so I relaunched inline with agents reading audit2-args.json.
   - Default throw view initially showed an odd recoil. It now reads "The car flies 28.1 m. Rex gets shoved backward at 21.9 m/s."

Open https://claude.ai/artifact/YFpbHtX8tM2Qwffd6znbZP (version 3). It's currently set to "Anyone with the link". I didn't change that; you can switch it in the page's Share menu.

**Status:** done. All fixes from the third review are in, tested, pushed to `claude/dinosaur-strength-physics-8o13ft` in lodge-docs (commit `a5795ee`, folder `rex-strength-lab/`), and republished at the same link. No PR opened.

**What the sim shows about Rex:**
1. **The ground gives out before Rex does.** Above record-human strength, heavy lifts sink his feet or crush the object. More strength doesn't help, because both failures depend only on the object's weight.
2. **Newton's third law dominates throws.** Default case: the car flies 28.1 m, and Rex gets shoved backward at 21.9 m/s. To stay put he has to dig his claws in or be bolted down.
3. **Sprinting is capped by friction, not strength.** His 0–100 km/h time stops improving past a point, because his grip depends only on his weight.
4. **A strong stomp launches Rex himself.** It pushes his body up as hard as his foot down, so at high strength he goes into the sky unless he's bolted.
5. **Real muscle vs comic book.** Real muscle caps limb speed: a jump of about 7 m, a fist of about 17 m/s, however strong he gets. Comic mode keeps getting faster up to near light speed, where every punch is a fireball.

**What the third review fixed (biggest first):**
- The sources table showed its links as plain text. It now has 222 working links.
- At ∞ strength, real muscle threw worse than at any finite strength. It now matches the top of the dial, and a test checks this.
- Real-muscle pitches falsely said "the ground gives way". The footing load now uses the average push over the throw instead of the peak.
- The strength slider took 110–170 ms per step. It now takes about 25–30 ms.
- About 30 smaller wording, chart and accessibility fixes.

**Checks:** all calibration tests pass. The full sweep (5,184 setting combinations) found 0 NaN or negative values, and 672 page states showed no broken text or console errors. All three review reports are now in the repo under `research/reviews/`.

**Limits that remain (also listed in the README):**
- Muscle shares are fitted to record athletes, not measured.
- The ground model ignores ice sheets snapping, layered soil and debris thrown up.
- Craters past a few hundred km are rough estimates.
- Flight counts only Earth's gravity, so arcs past the Moon are rough.
- Thrown objects would melt at the speeds shown; the sim doesn't model that.

Also maybe adding in Rex’s boyfriend, Ollie, who is equally as overpowered and indestructible, for two person simulations. This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - Original project: build the "Rex Super-Strength Lab". It simulates an indestructible, inexhaustible plush dinosaur (Rex) doing physics of famous feats of strength, at strengths from the strongest human to infinite, and shows forces, what he can lift or throw, and effects on his surroundings. This was done earlier, with 3 audit rounds; commit a5795ee is pushed and the artifact is published.
   - **Current request (latest user message):** "New feature: adding density and weight, and the effect that would have on the environment. Like if Rex were the density of a neutron star. Also maybe adding in Rex’s boyfriend, Ollie, who is equally as overpowered and indestructible, for two person simulations. (Arm wrestling, regular wrestling, games of catch, unstoppable force vs immovable objects)". The user attached an image of Ollie: a plush bull-man with horns, nose ring, leather vest, cargo pants and laced boots (no claws). Rex is shown as a dark scaly kaiju with orange spines.
   - Standing preferences:
     - Act as a professional critic, not a cheerleader; loyalty only to factual accuracy, clarity and intellectual honesty.
     - Say "I don't know" or "I cannot verify this" when information is lacking; admit mistakes briefly; no filler niceties.
     - "Always run in ADHD Mode": i-have-adhd rules are lead with the action, number steps, cap lists at 5, no preamble or recap, restate state, give specific time estimates, end with one concrete next action.
   - Constraints:
     - Develop on branch `claude/dinosaur-strength-physics-8o13ft` in lodge-docs; push with `git push -u origin <branch>`; do NOT create a PR unless asked.
     - Commit messages end with:
       Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
       Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01SsJhZqR8L4f82P9Dfpr4zn
     - No model identifiers in artifacts or code.
     - Ultracode is on: use workflows for substantive tasks; concurrency is 2 agents.
     - Don't invent canon for Ollie beyond the image. Default him to Rex's size, mass and strength, with his own adjustable settings.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Density = m / V, with V = 0.18·(H/2)³ m³ (BASE_V). Equal-volume radius R = (3V/4π)^(1/3) (0.3503 m at 2 m). Black-hole density 3c²/(8πGR²) is 1.31e27 kg/m³ at 2 m.
   - Self-gravity:
     - g_s = GM/R²; v_esc = √(2GM/R); dBeat = √(GM/g)
     - Bondi radius GM/a0², rate 4πλG²M²ρ/c³ with λ = 0.625 (rough)
     - rCrush = ρ_rock·GM/σ; Jeans 6×v_rms; tidal tension at 10 m = 80·Δa/8
     - atmosphere loss time = 5.1e18 kg / Bondi rate
   - PREM Earth model, gravity tunnel ≈ 38 min (Klotz 2015).
   - 3-D RK4 fall through a rotating Earth:
     - buoyancy, Poncelet ρv² drag, and rock strength (1.7 GPa, range 0.1–4.1 GPa) as a friction impulse
     - Ostriker (1999) dynamical friction F = 4πG²m²ρI(M)/v² (c_s = 6 km/s, lnΛ = 5)
     - orbit-averaged settling
   - Planet regimes: reshapes (≥ 1e-3 M_E), earthFalls (≥ M_E), blackHole. Their energies are floors.
   - Contests: Newton's third law; footing via anchorCapacity; arm force 25% of strength (estimate, 10–40%); the table carries the push until latCap (5 kN × sT²) is exceeded, then feet-only; pinning via pushApart on forearm effective mass; walk-out; shove; lift; throw.
   - Collisions:
     - relativistic headOn with splat and bounce bounds; contactForces (plush squash, matter 36.1 km/s, light-limit)
     - held test per bound; boltsLate regime (stress wave c_rock·t vs charger mass)
     - run-up speed u = u_drag·√(1 − e^(−2kx/m))
     - dipole rock load; unlimited momentum cases
   - Catch: aimed throws (aimEasy/aimHard over flyTo), catch over 0.3H stroke, Sutton–Graves heating, gravity wells (patched), fireball sweep m/(ρ0A).
   - Artifact page contract (tokens with dark mode, Google Fonts, phone width), Playwright screenshots, Node tests.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **/home/user/dino-strength-sim/src/engine.js** (main physics; heavily extended)
     - K additions: `G: 6.6743e-11`, `M_E: 5.9722e24`. `BASE_V = 0.18`, `bodyVolume(H)`. makeBody adds `volume, rho: m/volume`.
     - Self-gravity helpers: `eqRadius(body)`, `blackHoleDensity(H)`, `isBlackHole(body)`, `mutualGravity(bA,bB,d)` → {d, dContact, F, vEsc, Ebind}, `fallTogether(bA,bB,d0,d1)` → {t, vRel, E}.
     - Density section (inserted before "Moves"):
       - `W8` constants: OMEGA_E, SIGMA_ROCK 1.7e9, RHO_ROCK 2700, UCS_ROCK 2e8, R_AIR, NQ {sand 18.40, gravel 64.19}, WALK_LOAD 1.2, JEANS 6, E_NM, P_NM, RHO_OSMIUM 22587, M_RESHAPE 1e-3·M_E, SIGMA_LOW 0.1e9, SIGMA_HIGH 4.1e9, CS_ROCK 6000, BONDI_LAMBDA 0.625
       - PREM table and functions
       - `bodyGravity(body)` (includes tidal10 via d10Tension, atmosphereLossT, rCrush, rCrushUnconfined, tidal1g, decompJ)
       - `infallFrom`, `moveCheck(F,m)` (stand 1.4F ≥ W, walk 1.4F ≥ 1.2W, run F > W)
       - `groundUnderWeight` → regimes comic/stands/sinks/outOfSight/punchesThrough/fallsThrough, plus strongRockHolds/weakRockFails/rockCap
       - `dfI(M)` and `dfCoef(m,rho,v)` (Ostriker)
       - `fallThrough(body,{record,full,tMax,sigma,k,noDF,noDrag,latDeg})`:
         - innermost-pass detection requires `minR < 0.5*RE`
         - dt = `Math.min((RE - r < 20e3) ? 1 : (vrel > 100 ? 3 : 10), Math.max(1e-3, 0.002 * Math.max(r, 1e6) / Math.max(v, 1)))`
       - `settle(body,Amax,{sigma,k,noDF})`, `planetRegime(m,grav)` (eLowIsFloor)
       - `weight(ctx,{record})`, cached; it computes fall, settle, energyJ, stuckRange, shortRange, settleRange, gravDragDominant
     - Helpers: `selfPull`, `selfGravityOn(body)` (G m/(0.5H)² ≥ 1e-3 g), `heldRadius(body,obj)`, `escapeSpeedFrom`, `vInfinity`.
     - lift():
       - `gSelf`; W = m(g + gSelf); `move = moveCheck`
       - canLift requires move.stand
       - returns cantStand, standNeedKg, selfPullG
     - throwOnce():
       - `holdLoad = mB*g + obj.m*gSelf`
       - r0 = max(eqRadius, 0.25H); escapeNeeded; vOut; fallsBack; rMax; landsNear
       - `ctx.noFlight` option skips the flight
     - Contest section:
       - constants: `AW {forceFrac: 0.25, lever 0.19, effMass, pinAngle, elbowLoad 0.036, holdArm}`, `TABLE {refH 1.7562, depth 0.660, elbowCap 10e3, slamJ 102, latCap 5e3}`, RING_D 4.55, HUMERUS_NM 190
       - helpers: sameForce, footingOf, groundTear, shoveShare, shoveDrive
       - `armWrestle`: tableLat, tableBreaks, A = tableBreaks ? min(P,R) : P
       - `pushMatch`: holdOf2 lying rule, canLiftA/B, undefinedPush when both bolted and either F is ∞
       - `shoveOnce` (undefinedPush, fAwhole for the shover's slide), `shove`, `shoveBoth`
       - `liftPartner`: Fg = max(overhead, 0.385·G mA mB/dC²)
       - `throwPartner`: bolting-aware vEsc, vApart, fallsBack, heavierPartner, sinks

       - `collide(cA,cB,{source,gb,bounce})`: held per bound, heldOnlyIfSquishy, boltsLate (+ out.bolts {Eground,total,crater}), unlimitedVsBolted ('closedSystem' | 'rockGives' | 'planetMoves'), Elocal, KA, airStopsHim, airRunUp capped, outcome includes 'boltsLate'
     - `CATCHGAME` IIFE (ported from flyto.js + catch2.js):
       - CATCH constants, MATERIALS, OBJ_MATERIAL, flyTo (hStop, xStop, Rn heating)
       - aimEasy (cached), aimHard, farthest, releaseTable (uses noFlight ctx), wells, wellPath, catchIt, heatVerdict, fireballAt
       - `leg`: plus a 'no-arc' result when the lob overshoots
       - tossPartner, game, partnerAsObject, pushStartRadius
     - Exports include:
       - BASE_V, bodyVolume, eqRadius, blackHoleDensity, isBlackHole, mutualGravity, fallTogether
       - W8, PREM, premRho, premG, premPhi, premSolid, bodyGravity, infallFrom, moveCheck, groundUnderWeight, fallThrough, settle, planetRegime, weight, selfPull, escapeSpeedFrom, vInfinity
       - AW, TABLE, RING_D, HUMERUS_NM, armWrestle, pushMatch, shove, shoveBoth, liftPartner, throwPartner
       - CATCH, flyTo, catchGame, catchLeg, tossPartner, catchIt, partnerAsObject, catchMaterials, `catchMinD: (bT,bC,obj) => pushStartRadius(bT)+heldRadius(bC,obj)+0.3*bC.H+1`
       - COL, headOn, standoff, chargeSpeed, collide, holdOf, rockLoad, contactForces

     - HTML: density field; Ollie `<details id="ollie-setup">` with `__DUO_IMG__`; group seg `#grp-solo/#grp-duo`.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - In-page `const NAMES` clash (already used for number names): renamed the duo map to `WHO`.
   - Python patch assertions failed when anchors didn't match (the gravity bullet's leading "} else if"; the paradox bullet's leading "if (...)"). Fixed by using the exact substring and rerunning the whole patch.
   - fallThrough was slow (up to 1 s) at 1e11–1e12 kg. Fixed with an r-floor dt, the 3 s cap, averaged settling after the first pass, and full 3-D only when depthShort > 0.3 R_E.
   - The settle "remainder" missed elapsed time. Fixed by adding fall.t.
   - Turnaround hysteresis used a stale speed (depthShort 0). Fixed: plain prevVr plus a `minR < 0.5*RE` requirement.
   - A BHL drag first attempt gave wrong low-speed behaviour. Replaced with Ostriker dynamical friction. The no-drag test now uses the `noDrag` option.
   - The catch lob to the antipode picked an escaping arc. Added the 'no-arc' result.
   - Doubled article ("the the concrete slab"). Added the `theSurf()` helper.
   - logBars clipped long values. padR is now computed from value-text width.
   - The weightshot output was stale because preview.html is only regenerated by `node test/shots.js`. I now run shots.js after each build.

5. Problem Solving:
   - All four designs were adversarially checked. The contest, density and collide critiques are fully applied in the engine and page. Key results after the fixes:
     - Hulk-vs-Hulk arm wrestling breaks the table at about 6.5 kN, then becomes a feet-only dead heat at 1.06 kN. On comic ground, strength decides.
     - Neutron-star Rex: first trip 38.2 min, turns back 5.3 m short (range 2.8–8.5 m), 809 km west, settles in 126 years (range 81–29,000).
     - White-dwarf Rex sticks about 216 km from the centre (range 0–646 km).
     - Default collide: run-up 19.3 m gives 14.7 m/s.
   - The browser sweep (an older build, before the critique fixes) covered 1,512 states with 0 bad text and 0 errors.
   - **Catch critique (just read, NOT yet applied).** Required fixes:
     1. Critical: hand inertia. Use a first-contact inelastic collision with m_h = 2×handEff (7.9 kg at default), energy ½μv² absorbed over a palm give of 2–5 cm (estimate). The stroke then stops m + m_h from v·m/(m + m_h). Base the baseball and grip checks on the peak contact force.
     2. Critical: a survival gate before 'caught'. The object breaks up in flight when ρ(h)v² exceeds crush strength (Collins 2005); heat 'destroyed' uses the plasma wording; if F/A_front exceeds crush, the verdict is "stops the wreckage". Rename 'Clean catch' to "His arms can stop it" and never show it next to "Hands punch into it".
     3. Relativistic classes: 'arrives' becomes a white-hot plasma/debris front with no hand catch (momentum push only); 'before' is an order-of-magnitude blast; use a relativistic snowplow for γ ≫ 1.
     4. Sliding friction: use anc.Rslide(F) by bisection when the catcher slips; include gravity along the path (v_eff² += 2 g d sin γ); pass the full line force to N(F); add Ollie's weight to the foot load in the partner toss.
     5. Drag on dense-partner straight-line flights (integrate it; bisect the launch speed); flag drag when its energy exceeds 1% of launch energy.
     6. Radiation: show heat as a range (convection only to plus σT⁴); flag from about 8 km/s or nose > 1 m; never call it an "upper bound".
     7. Page text: print ½mv²/d only when he doesn't slip; cut or fix the mitt sentence.
     8. Consistent reach geometry: chest at max(eqRadius, 0.07H) + L/2, hands 0.3H further out.
     9. Environmental effects: drag energy near the thrower and catcher via blastBlock, sonic boom at the catcher, catch energy in TNT.
     10. Object size: when it is larger than the catcher, "lands on and around him".
     11. Minor: v_L = 0 "just lets go" for a dense catcher without a hump; 'unreachable' wording when air limits a fastball; no-air comparison with Δh; add push.t to the round trip; subsonic Cd for slides; limestone 2.5 MJ/kg; Adair p. 28; extrapolated flag below 2,145 m/s; skin sentence → "the heat reaching it could melt under 1% of it (rough)"; shuttle tiles note.

Build: cd /home/user/dino-strength-sim && python3 build-data.py && node build.js && node test/shots.js   (makes dist/index.html and dist/preview.html).

text:
Status: catch-game fixes are done and tested; the final audit and the full browser sweep are running.

**Catch-game fixes, now in the engine and on the page:**
1. **Hand inertia.** Ollie's hands and forearms weigh 7.9 kg and start at rest. A lobbed baseball now spends 98% of its energy hitting his palms (115–286 N) instead of in a soft 60 cm give.
2. **Fastball baseball.** The first hit on his palms squeezes it 21–53× harder than a home-run hit, so it now reads "probably bursts". It used to read "survives".
3. **Things that can't be caught:**
   - Anything torn apart by air pressure. Example: the pyramid thrown across the planet.
   - Anything burnt up on the way.
   - Anything bigger than Ollie. A bus is "too big".
   - Anything crushed even across its whole front. It becomes "stops the wreckage".
4. **Near light speed.** A relativistic pyramid now hits him as plasma and debris carrying almost all its momentum. It no longer gets a hand catch. The air between them takes 1.8 × 10²⁷ J of heat.
5. **Effects on the surroundings.** Each catch now shows:
   - how much energy the air takes, and how much of it lands near Rex and near Ollie
   - the shock wave at Ollie's hands
   - the catch energy in TNT
   - a blast-radius chart when the energy is large

**Other changes:**
- When Ollie slips, the slide now uses sliding friction.
- Drag now applies on the straight-line flights between dense partners. A neutron-star Ollie needs no throw at all: Rex just lets go.
- Air heating is now shown as a range up to a radiation ceiling.

**Checks so far:** all calibration tests pass, including 12 new catch tests. The engine sweep covered 290,636 cases with 0 problems. I also corrected about 20 source facts the earlier reviews flagged, for example the white-dwarf density range and the Adair page number.

**Still running:**
- Browser sweep of every tab across settings: about 1 hour.
- Final audit with four reviewers: physics, regressions, sources, page text and layout. A second reviewer re-checks every finding before I act on it.

Next: fix whatever the audit confirms, copy everything to lodge-docs, commit and push, then republish the page at the same link.

Rex's default height is set to 10 ft (3.048 m). His mass is still being estimated from the picture.

**What's in place (in the source, not built yet):**
- Rex and Ollie each get their own build, measured from the picture. A build is body volume, frontal area for air drag, and foot size, all scaled with height. That keeps density, gravity and drag consistent with the new size.
- The 2 m, 180 kg body the strength dial was calibrated on still exists. It's now a separate "Calibration body" size chip. The "Dino (2 m)" chip becomes "Rex (10 ft)". The engine tests still use the 2 m, 180 kg calibration body and pass.
- If your browser saved the old 2 m, 180 kg defaults, they switch to the new ones automatically.
- Ollie is measured from the same picture. If he comes out the same height, he defaults to 10 ft as well.

**One consequence to expect:** a heavy 10 ft Rex needs well over world-record-human strength just to stand up. Rex's weight will be several times his 2 m weight. The default dial (90.7 t) is far above that, so the default page is fine. Near the bottom of the dial he'll show "can't stand", which is correct physics, not a bug.

- **Mass estimate:** three independent methods plus a checker who re-measures and reconciles them.
- **Final audit:** about half done. One finding so far: a neutron-star Ollie's "can't hold it up" figure is really his own arm's weight, not the ball's.

A body-measurement calculator fits well alongside the strength lab. Plan:

text:
The final audit confirmed 54 findings, about 40 distinct issues once duplicates are merged. They're now being fixed.

**Worst ones:**
1. **Settling time wrong:** a units error makes a neutron-star Rex settle at the Earth's centre in about 130 years. It should be thousands of years, and the per-trip energy and quake size are inflated to match.
2. **Relativistic-catch blast too small:** it counts only the heat made in the air between them, not the energy that actually hits Ollie, so it wrongly shrinks as Ollie stands closer.
3. **Tabs disagree:** three tabs give different answers for the same unstoppable-force setup.
4. **Catch check misses contact:** a shot put crushed on contact still counts as "caught".
5. **Throw speeds near vertical wrong:** steep throws use launch speeds that are up to 190× too high.
6. **Wording contradictions,** including one that gives Ollie claws.

**Fixes in progress:** four fixers work one after another on the same files, in this order: weight tab, catch, collide and wrestle, arm wrestle and the rest. Each one rebuilds, runs the tests and adds a regression check for every serious fix. Two reviewers then re-run all 54 original reproductions against the final build.

**Rex and Ollie's size, provisional for now:**

| | Height | Mass | Volume |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rex | 10 ft | 2.45 t | 2.33 m³ |
| Ollie | 10 ft | 2.48 t | 2.36 m³ |

The three methods landed on 2.36, 2.49 and 2.47 t for Rex, with an overall range of about 2.0–2.9 t. A checker is reconciling them now, and the final numbers will move by a few percent at most.

**Build calculator:** research is still running.

**Next:**
1. Put in the final masses.
2. Check them against the arm-wrestling art, which shows arm depth from the side.
3. Rebuild and rerun every test and sweep.
4. Commit, push and republish.

Expect about 3–4 hours, most of it the fix workflow.

text:
Rex's default body is final: **10 ft (3.05 m), 2,700 kg**.

| | Rex | Ollie |
|---|---|---|
| Height | 10 ft | 10 ft (3.06 m to his horn tips, within measuring error) |
| Mass | 2,700 kg | 2,700 kg |
| Plausible range | 2,300–3,000 kg | 2,300–3,000 kg |
| Volume | 2.55 m³ | 2.55 m³ |
| Density | 1,060 kg/m³ | 1,060 kg/m³ |
| Facing area (air drag) | 4.4 m² | 4.5 m² |
| Foot sole, each | 0.31 m² (wide paws) | 0.15 m² (boots) |
| Weight | 26.5 kN | 26.5 kN |

**How the mass was estimated:**
- **Scale:** 10 ft set the scale at 790 pixels from Rex's crest tip to the floor, about 3.9 mm per pixel.
- **Slices:** each body was cut into 1-pixel slices, each treated as an oval. The depth of each oval came from US Army body-survey proportions (ANSUR II), adjusted for these bulkier builds.
- **Arms:** both arms were sized from the one we can fully see.
- **Tail:** includes the part hidden behind Rex's hips. It also accounts for the tail sitting about 10% farther from the camera.
- **Density:** 1,060 kg/m³ is the measured density of lean bodybuilders, minus some lung air (Fry, Cisar & Housh 1987).
- **What the range covers:** depth, arm, tail and density uncertainty.
- **Not covered:** dinosaur-style air sacs, which could make Rex about 7% lighter.

**Comparisons:**
- About 6.8× an average man scaled up to 10 ft.
- About 4× a 135 kg pro bodybuilder scaled to 10 ft.

**Consequences in the sim:**
- Ollie's boots carry the same weight on half Rex's sole area. On soft ground Ollie sinks first.

text:
The build-calculator research is done and checked, and the page is now being built in its own folder (`/home/user/build-calc`). The build workflow runs four stages:

1. **Compile the data.** Apply all 23 verifier corrections. Add US civilian averages, since the Army soldiers are leaner than the general public. Derive Rex's and Ollie's girths from their picture measurements.
2. **Build the page.** You pick a build and a height and get weight plus seven girths, each tagged measured, official, reported, derived or estimate. It also has a body diagram, comparison bars against an average man, and BMI and FFMI. A reverse mode takes typed-in girths and estimates weight two ways: from the soldier data, and from a body-volume model.
3. **Audit it twice:** once for numbers and model, once for page text and layout.
4. **Fix** whatever the audits confirm.

Expect the calculator to need a couple of hours more.

**Rex lab:** the audit-fix workflow is working through its four batches. After that come the description updates for the 10 ft, 2,700 kg bodies, then commit, push and republish.

text:
The build calculator is live and committed: https://claude.ai/artifact/9aKMVmtGqXXT2kGMYvZb5E

**What it does:**
- Pick a build and a height. You get weight plus chest, waist, flexed arm, forearm, thigh, calf and neck, in imperial or metric.
- Each number is tagged measured, official, reported, derived or estimate.
- It also shows BMI and FFMI, a body diagram, and comparison bars against an average man.
- Reverse mode estimates weight from girths you type in, two ways. On the US Army survey data it's accurate to about 1.6 kg.
- Characters beyond the measured human range get a warning. That covers most comic characters, Rex and Ollie. A switch can hide those girths instead.

**55 builds:**
- US Army soldiers and US adults
- natural and pro bodybuilders
- strongmen
- 21 comic characters
- Rex and Ollie

**Rex and Ollie, from the picture:**

| | Chest | Waist | Upper arm | Thigh | Calf |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rex | 3.45 m (136 in) | 2.59 m | 1.90 m | 1.92 m | 2.00 m |
| Ollie | 3.69 m | 3.50 m | 1.75 m | 1.99 m | 2.08 m |

- The chests probably read about 12% low. The same method undershoots on real soldiers.
- In the calculator, Ollie is listed at 3.06 m to his horn tips, the picture measurement. The Rex lab rounds him to 10 ft. Both are within measuring error.

**Checks:**
- 22 of 22 tests pass. They re-derive the survey statistics from the raw data.
- 31 audit findings fixed.
- Rex and Ollie now show as male, not "sex not stated". Rex is now a dinosaur build, not a lizard build.

**Committed:** `build-calculator/` in lodge-docs, commit 4a03723, pushed to `claude/dinosaur-strength-physics-8o13ft`. The page is private until you share it from its Share menu.

**Rex lab fixes:** 39 of 42 fixed so far, tests passing:
- weight tab: 15 of 15
- catch: 13 of 16
- collide and wrestle: 11 of 11

The last batch, arm wrestle and the remaining items, is running. After it, two reviewers re-check all 54 findings.

**Next:** when that finishes, I'll update the Rex lab descriptions for the 10 ft, 2,700 kg bodies, rerun every test and sweep, commit, push and republish.

text:
The audit-fix round is done: 49 of 54 findings are confirmed fixed and all 106 calibration checks pass.

**Fixed (the important ones):**
1. **Settling time:** a neutron-star Rex now settles at the Earth's centre in about 2,200 years (range 490 to 29,000), not 130. The per-trip energy dropped from trillions of tonnes of TNT to about a billion tonnes, with a magnitude 6.5 quake instead of 8.9.
2. **Relativistic catch blast:** it now counts the full energy released at Ollie, so it no longer shrinks as he stands closer.
3. **Contradictory tabs:** the three tabs that disagreed on the same unstoppable-force setup now agree.
4. **Crushed on contact:** a shot put crushed on contact is no longer "caught".
5. **Steep throws:** release speeds near vertical are no longer up to 190× too high.
6. **Ollie's claws:** his claws are gone from the collide text.

**One last fixer is working now** (then a re-checker):
1. Lob catches still report a meaningless stroke time, which makes the default round trip "about 33 s". After first contact Ollie can take as long as he likes to bring the ball in. The round trip will count only the throws and flights, and say so.
2. Side effects of the fixes: doubled wording, a "comes down steeply" line on level arrivals, and a gravity chip that prints "95,000,000,000".
3. Drift distances that are meaningless after Rex swings through the centre of the Earth.
4. Smaller wording leftovers.
5. **10 ft text updates:** the assumption cards, a "His build (default)" density chip, a sourced fact for the picture estimate, and the README.

**Left as a known limit:** a few long-distance catch lobs take 2–3 s to render. Shove went from 2.2 s to under 40 ms.

**Build Calculator:** live and committed.

**Next:** when the fixer and re-checker finish, I'll rerun the full engine sweep, copy everything to lodge-docs, commit, push and republish the Rex lab at the same link. Expect about an hour.
